World’s First: AutoFlight Nails a 5-eVTOL Autonomous Formation Flight in China
9 photos
Photo: AutoFlight
AutoFlight isn’t just another eVTOL (electric vertical takeoff and landing) maker. It has developed a 2-ton eVTOL that comes in two configurations (the cargo CarryAll, and the firefighting CarryAll), as well as a 5-ton eVTOL (the Matrix), and all of these flew together recently in what is claimed to be the world’s first 5-eVTOL formation flight.
On October 31 and November 1, a few alumni representatives from the Stanford Executive Program (SEP) at Stanford Graduate School of Business were among the lucky guests who had the opportunity to watch a global premiere related to eVTOL technology. Five eVTOL in two different weight classes flew together seamlessly, without any pilot onboard.
One was a 5-ton V5000 Matrix, and the other four were in the 2-ton class, across two different models (the V2000CG CarryAll cargo and the V2000CGF CarryAll firefighting). These five AutoFlight aircraft completed a coordinated, fully autonomous flight for 47 minutes, with the V5000 Matrix (which acted as the lead) covering more than 1433 km (82.6 miles).
This extraordinary demonstration took place in Kunshan, China, where AutoFlight operates its Bailian Lake Flight Test Base. Apart from the Stanford alumni representatives, AutoFlight customers and players in the international eVTOL industry were also invited to attend. And there was even more excitement when all of them got to watch the formation flight in the most unique way, while onboard AutoFlight’s futuristic floating vertiport, the Sunship.
The Chinese AAM company has been working its way to this global premiere. Earlier this year, it completed a three-aircraft formation demonstration. That flight was carried out by one 5-ton Matrix and two 2-ton Prosperity eVTOLs. Building on the success of that May demonstration , this recent formation flight took things to the next level, especially considering the challenging wind conditions on the second day.
The point of all this is to take steps toward autonomous multi-aircraft operations in the future, and building transport networks that could connect long-haul, regional, and last-mile routes. It’s a much more complex vision of AAM (Advanced Air Mobility) than basic air taxi service and cargo. The ability to successfully coordinate eVTOL of different sizes and with different roles, all flying without a pilot, requires incredible planning and safety management.
Just as impressive as the aircraft themselves is AutoFlight’s Sunship, one of the most futuristic vertiport concepts. Defined as a water-based green vertiport, this floating platform runs on electric power, with solar power for range extension, and supports fast eVTOL charging.
It was developed for high efficiency across five applications, from urban commuting, sea-air tourism, and emergency response, to the industry of offshore energy, and mobile airports (multiple Sunships connected together to form a distributed vertiport system).
AutoFlight’s Prosperity eVTOL for passenger transportation is on its way to full certification, while the cargo CarryAll version is already the first in its category (2-ton class) to be fully certified.
